intro: Formal phone calls: switchboards, extensions, customer service and everything that goes wrong on the line.
p.poner con.consejo: It is asked like this: «¿me pone con el señor Ruiz?». «Pasar con» also works.
p.extensión.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -ión: «la extensión». The x sounds «ks»: eks-ten-SYON.
p.no se retire.consejo: It is a formal command with «usted». «Retirarse» here means hanging up or leaving the phone.
p.atención al cliente.consejo: It is feminine: «la atención al cliente». It is the service you call with a problem.
p.centralita.consejo: It is feminine and comes from «central». It ends in -ita, but it is the normal name.
p.comunicar.consejo: You say «está comunicando» when the line is busy. It also means «to give a piece of news».
p.cortarse.consejo: It is pronominal: «se ha cortado la llamada». Also: «me he cortado» with a knife.
p.cobertura.consejo: It is feminine: «la cobertura». You say «no hay cobertura» in a place without signal.
p.llamada perdida.consejo: It is feminine: «una llamada perdida». «Perdida» agrees with «llamada».
p.devolver la llamada.consejo: The o becomes «ue»: «devuelvo». You say «dígale que me devuelva la llamada».
p.buzón de voz.consejo: It is masculine: «el buzón de voz». The z in «buzón» sounds like th.
p.dar de baja.consejo: Its opposite is «dar de alta»: starting a service. The j in «baja» sounds like h.
p.avería.consejo: It has an accent on the í to keep the i and the a apart: a-be-RI-a. It is feminine.
p.colgar.consejo: The o becomes «ue»: «cuelgo», «cuelgas». People used to hang the receiver up for real.
b1.texto:
A company answers with its name: **Seguros Faro, ¿dígame?**

**Asking for someone.** **¿Me pone con** el señor Ruiz, por favor? **¿Me pasa con** la extensión 204? **Quisiera hablar con** el departamento de ventas.

**The answers.**

- **¿De parte de quién?**
- **No se retire, por favor.** **Ahora le paso.**
- **Está comunicando.** (the line is busy)
- **¿Desea dejar algún recado?**

**Leaving a message.** **Dígale que me devuelva la llamada.** An indirect order with **que** takes the subjunctive.

**Problems.** **Se ha cortado.** **No hay cobertura.** **Me ha saltado el buzón de voz.** **Tengo tres llamadas perdidas tuyas.**

**With the company.** You call **atención al cliente** to **dar de baja** a service or to report **una avería**.

On the phone you address people formally: **le** paso, no **le** puede atender, ¿desea dejar**le** un recado?
b2.f0.texto: Faro Insurance, how can I help?
b2.f1.texto: Could you put me through to the faults department, please?
b2.f3.texto: Thank you, I will wait here.
b2.f4.texto: The line is busy right now.
b2.f5.texto: Would you like to leave a message?
b2.f6.texto: Tell them to call me back as soon as possible.
b2.f8.texto: I have been without a line for three days.
b2.f9.texto: If they do not fix it this week, I will cancel the service.
b4.texto:
On the phone you address people as **usted** and use the pronoun **le**:

- **Ahora le paso.** **No le puede atender.** **¿Desea dejarle un recado?**
- Formal command: **no se retire**, **espere un momento**.
- An indirect order with **que** takes the subjunctive: **dígales que me devuelvan la llamada**.
- **Quisiera** + infinitive to ask politely: **quisiera hablar con ventas**.
- For problems: **se ha cortado**, **no hay cobertura**.
b4.e0.texto: I will put you through to the director now.
b4.e1.texto: Tell him to call me this afternoon.
b4.e2.texto: I would like to speak to the sales department.
b5.f0.texto: Marcos holds the phone against his ear and looks at the white ceiling.
b5.f1.texto: A piano tune repeats the same melody over and over.
b5.f2.texto: Outside, the afternoon turns grey over the wet roofs.
b5.f3.texto: On the table, a cup of coffee goes cold beside a pile of bills.
b5.f4.texto: Suddenly the melody cuts off with a dry click.
b5.f5.texto: A woman's voice greets calmly from the other end of the line.
b5.f6.texto: Marcos explains his problem in short, clear sentences.
b5.f7.texto: On the other end, some keys sound with a calm rhythm.
b5.f8.texto: The woman promises an answer before Friday.
b5.f9.texto: Marcos hangs up slowly and leaves the phone on the pile of bills.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: an indirect order with «que» takes the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is indicative; an indirect order asks for the subjunctive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The future does not work for an indirect order.
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is not about journalists: it is about the line.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Yes: someone is already using that line.
b8.o0.refuerzo: With «con», «dar» is not used to connect calls.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «poner con» is connecting to someone else.
b8.o2.refuerzo: You are not asking to be called: you are asking to be connected.
b8.pregunta: Complete the request with the right verb.
b9.frase: En este momento no le puede atender
b9.traduccion: He cannot attend to you at the moment
b10.o1.refuerzo: That is the opposite: starting a service.
b10.o2.refuerzo: That is calling back whoever called you.
b10.pregunta: You want to cancel the contract. What do you want to do?
b12.o0.refuerzo: It is not about the rate, but about the call.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the connection has suddenly cut off.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Leaving a message is something else.
b12.pregunta: What has happened if you say «Se ha cortado»?
p.seguros.consejo: In a phone greeting, the company name comes first. Plural form here.
p.dígame.consejo: A polite phrase to answer a call: «dígame», go ahead.
p.departamento.consejo: A section of a company, like sales or support.
p.averías.consejo: The v sounds like b. The stress falls on «RI».
p.desea.consejo: A polite way to ask what someone wants: «¿desea...?»
p.dígales.consejo: «les» means to them. It attaches to the subjunctive verb.
p.arreglan.consejo: «arreglar» means to repair or fix. The g is hard before a.
p.daré.consejo: Future of «dar». The accent on é marks the stress.
p.servicio.consejo: «dar de baja» means to cancel a subscription.
p.dígale.consejo: «le» means to him or to her, the polite form.
p.ventas.consejo: From «vender», to sell. The v sounds like b.
p.facturas.consejo: Papers listing what is owed. From «factura».
p.chasquido.consejo: A short, sharp sound, like a snap.
p.cortas.consejo: Its opposite is «largas», long. It agrees with «frases».
p.teclas.consejo: The buttons of a keyboard or phone. The c before l sounds like k.
p.atender.glosa: to attend to, to take a call (atender)
p.atender.consejo: «atender» means to take care of someone, often on the phone.
p.interrumpido.consejo: With «se ha», it describes a call that was cut off.
